children: Muhurat Trading Reflects Positive Market Sentiment As Leading Stocks Advance Despite Selective Selling Pressure

Indian equity markets continued their upward momentum during the special Muhurat Trading session on Sunday, held on the occasion of Diwali, extending their gains for the seventh consecutive session. Tata Steel, Sun Pharma and Hindalco featured among the leading gainers, while SBI Life, IndiGo and Infosys were among the top laggards.

Tata Steel emerged as the biggest gainer among the stocks listed, rising 2.29 per cent, or Rs 4.27, to Rs 190.57. The stock recorded a trading volume of 76.07 lakh shares, with a total turnover of Rs 145.06 crore.

Sun Pharma followed with a 1.93 per cent gain, adding Rs 35.90 to reach Rs 1,895.90. The stock recorded a turnover of Rs 33.01 crore during the session. TMPV advanced 0.89 per cent to Rs 294.60, while Hindalco gained 0.86 per cent to trade at Rs 966.65. ONGC also ended higher, rising 0.85 per cent to Rs 233.74, with a total traded value of Rs 44.28 crore.

Among the laggards, SBI Life recorded the steepest decline, falling 0.84 per cent, or Rs 14.90, to Rs 1,769.10. Its total traded value stood at Rs 4.87 crore. IndiGo declined 0.68 per cent, or Rs 37.30, to Rs 5,438.70. Infosys slipped 0.54 per cent to Rs 1,175, while Bharti Airtel lost 0.51 per cent to close at Rs 2,096.50. Trent ended 0.42 per cent lower at Rs 3,066.

Commenting on the outlook for Samvat 2083, Raamdeo Agrawal, Chairman and Co-Founder of Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said, “After two years of stagnation, market has the potential to give investors bumper returns by next Diwali, because of confluence of low valuation and high earnings growth.”
“Potential crash in oil prices, stable currency, return of foreign investors, moderation of AI hype and broad-based earnings growth will support higher valuation multiples. Happy Diwali!” he said.

Agrawal identified lower crude oil prices, currency stability and renewed foreign investor participation as factors that could support the market over the coming year. He also highlighted moderation in AI-related market enthusiasm and broader earnings growth as potential drivers of higher valuation multiples.
